title: Security Audit Report
subtitle: Production readiness review for Acme Commerce Platform

findings.title: API keys hardcoded in Docker image
findings.impact: Anyone with image access can extract Stripe, SendGrid, and Twilio API keys. Full access to payment, email, and SMS services.
findings.recommendation: Use Docker secrets or runtime env injection. Rotate all exposed keys immediately. Never bake secrets into images.

findings.title: SQL injection in product search endpoint
findings.impact: Attackers can read, modify, or delete any data in the database via crafted search queries.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries via Prisma's where clause. Never concatenate user input into raw SQL.

findings.title: Authentication bypass on admin endpoints
findings.impact: 6 admin API endpoints have no auth guard. Anyone can access user management, order refunds, and system config.
findings.recommendation: Add JwtAuthGuard + AdminGuard to all admin routes. Add integration test verifying 401 on unauthenticated requests.

findings.title: Rate limiting missing on login and registration
findings.impact: Brute force attacks on login can succeed. Credential stuffing at scale with no throttling.
findings.recommendation: Add @nestjs/throttler with 10 attempts per minute on login, 3 per hour on registration. Add Redis-backed throttler for distributed rate limiting.

findings.title: CORS configured to allow all origins
findings.impact: Any website can make authenticated cross-origin requests to the API. Enables CSRF-style attacks from malicious sites.
findings.recommendation: Whitelist specific domains: localhost, acme.shop, admin.acme.shop. Use config-based origin list for environment flexibility.

findings.title: User session tokens never expire
findings.impact: Stolen JWT tokens are valid forever. No way to revoke access without secret rotation.
findings.recommendation: Set access token expiry to 15min, refresh token to 24h. Implement refresh token rotation with reuse detection.

findings.title: File upload accepts arbitrary MIME types
findings.impact: Users can upload executable files, HTML with scripts, or malicious payloads. Stored files served directly could execute XSS.
findings.recommendation: Whitelist allowed MIME types (image/jpeg, image/png, application/pdf). Validate file signatures, not just headers. Strip metadata from images.

findings.title: Password policy too weak
findings.impact: Users can set easily guessable passwords like '123456' or 'password'. Vulnerable to dictionary attacks.
findings.recommendation: Require min 10 chars, 1 uppercase, 1 number, 1 special char. Check against HaveIBeenPwned API. Use class-validator decorators.

findings.title: No audit log for admin actions
findings.impact: No traceability for sensitive operations like refunds, user deletion, or config changes. Cannot investigate incidents.
findings.recommendation: Create AuditLog entity. Log all admin mutations with actor, action, target, before/after, timestamp, IP. Add admin UI to view logs.

findings.title: Error responses include stack traces in production
findings.impact: Internal implementation details, file paths, and library versions leaked to API consumers. Aids attackers in reconnaissance.
findings.recommendation: Set NestJS to production mode. Use a global exception filter that returns generic messages with error codes. Log full errors server-side only.

findings.title: PII stored in plain text logs
findings.impact: Emails, phone numbers, and partial card numbers appear in application logs. GDPR violation if logs are shared or retained.
findings.recommendation: Implement a log sanitization pipe that masks PII fields. Use structured logging with redaction. Review all log statements for PII.

findings.title: Missing security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options)
findings.impact: No Content-Security-Policy allows inline scripts. No HSTS means downgrade attacks. Clickjacking possible without X-Frame-Options.
findings.recommendation: Add header directives in Caddyfile: CSP with strict-dynamic, HSTS with 1-year max-age, X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff.

findings.title: Dependencies not pinned, 4 known CVEs
findings.impact: Minor version updates can introduce breaking changes. 4 dependencies have known CVEs (2 medium, 2 low).
findings.recommendation: Pin all dependencies to exact versions. Run pnpm audit in CI. Update vulnerable packages. Add Dependabot or Renovate for automated PRs.

findings.title: Database backups not encrypted
findings.impact: If backup storage is compromised, all user data is accessible in plain text.
findings.recommendation: Encrypt backups with AES-256 using a managed KMS key. Store encryption keys separately from backup storage. Test restore from encrypted backup.

strengths: Payment processing uses Stripe webhook signature verification with idempotency keys, preventing replay attacks
Password hashing uses bcrypt with cost factor 12, exceeding OWASP minimum recommendations
All database queries go through Prisma ORM with parameterized queries (except the one SQL injection finding)
TLS 1.3 enforced across all environments with perfect forward secrecy
Role-based access control is enforced at both route guard and service layer level
API rate limiting is implemented on payment and checkout endpoints using Redis-backed throttler

verdict.title: NOT READY FOR PRODUCTION
verdict.subtitle: 3 critical vulnerabilities must be resolved before launch
